tweets: A malicious contract can call back into the caller before the first function invocation finishes.
This allows different invocations of the same function to interact in undesirable ways.
The best practice is to perform all internal state changes before executing the external call.
This ordering approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.
Using a reentrancy lock, such as OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard, is also recommended.
